supported_design_issues: Declared closure omits combine/report but graph_example claims both; emit action lacks its node.
Parent-only inspection cannot discover unrequested descendants; see semantic_counterexample.json.
Only intervention receives actual dependency graph despite matched-input claim.
Correctness oracle uses damaged declared graph instead of actual task semantics.
Development/held-out call scopes are unspecified; 72 calls is required only if both six-instance partitions get 3*2 model plans.
Generator topology, operators, scenario injection and prompt-condition definitions remain unspecified.
E-versus-F primary endpoint can pass while A=E falsification condition fails; separate the two claims.
audit_corrections: The invalid action is emit without node; extra retry/error fields are not required by graph schema.
Actual graph access can be a legitimate shared input; the issue is unequal information, not automatic numerical oracle leakage.
Self-authored held-out data are allowed when labeled and frozen; external independence is not claimed.
A null-effect retry negative control is legitimate but cannot show retry benefits.
The composite correctness/cost endpoint is falsifiable; small sample precision and the A comparison are separate limitations.
The statement that development necessarily requires 36 additional calls is stronger than the incomplete proposal supports.

token_policy.reason: Omitting max_tokens resulted in observed provider-default length cutoff at 8192; use provider maximum capacity instead.
